tone_statements.citation: 李雲兵 [Li Yunbing]. 2003. 苗瑤語聲調問題 [Issues in the tones of the Miao-Yao (Hmong-Mien) languages]. Language and Linguistics 語言暨語言學 4(4): 683-712. Taipei: Institute of Linguistics, Academia Sinica.
tone_statements.quote: (9) 廣西金秀縣長垌鄉龍華村話，屬苗語支炯奈語長垌方言，簡稱長垌。 [...] 苗語支語言入聲並入舒聲的現象比較普遍，又如布努語瑙格勞方言包諾土語芒降的 D1 調並入 C1 調，巴哼語 D2 並入 B2 或 C2，優諾語 D2 調並入 C2，炯奈語 D 並入 B，畬語 B2、C2 合併，等等，不再一一舉例。
tone_statements.translation: (9) The speech of Longhua village, Changdong township, Jinxiu county, Guangxi, belonging to the Changdong dialect of Jiongnai (Hmongic branch), abbreviated 'Changdong'. [...] The merger of checked (入聲) tones into non-checked tones is fairly common in Hmongic-branch languages; e.g. in Mangjiang (Baonuo vernacular of the Naogelao dialect of Bunu) tone D1 has merged into C1, in Pa-Hng D2 into B2 or C2, in Younuo D2 into C2, in Jiongnai D has merged into B, in She B2 and C2 have merged, and so on.
tone_statements.locator: p.685 (materials list, item 9) and p.703, section 3.1 (end), Language and Linguistics 4.4
tone_statements.summary: Jiongnai (Longhua) has the Hmong-Mien register-split tone-category system (A1-D2); per Li the historical checked category *D has merged into B after loss of stop codas; no tone values given here (the 8-value inventory 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12 is in Mao & Li 2002, known/print).

tone_statements.citation: 田口善久 [Taguchi, Yoshihisa]. 1996. 炯奈話調査報告 [A study on Jiong Nai dialect]. 言語文化論叢 (Papers on languages and cultures, Chiba University) 2: 17-24.
tone_statements.quote: 1.2 声調 陳（1991）によると、炯奈話（竜華村）の声調は以下のようである。上段に声調番号を、下段に調値をしめす。 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 / 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12 一方、六巷村の声調は以下のようである。 1 2 3 4 5 6 7a 7b 8 / 44 42 35 54 33 31 43 55 21 以上のように、第1声調と第7（の一部）、第8声調はほぼ同じ調値であるほかは、調値に大きな違いが見られる。第2、第3、第5、第6声調においては昇降平のパターンも一致しない。また、六巷村の第4声調は極めて高いpitchから始まる声調で、少し低く発音すると第2声調に聞き取られてしまう。 …
tone_statements.translation: 1.2 Tones. According to Chen (1991) the tones of Jiongnai (Longhua village) are as follows; upper row = tone number, lower row = tone value: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 / 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12. The tones of Liuxiang village, on the other hand, are: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7a 7b 8 / 44 42 35 54 33 31 43 55 21. As seen, apart from tone 1, (part of) tone 7 and tone 8 having nearly the same values, the values differ greatly; in tones 2, 3, 5 and 6 even the rising/falling/level patterns do not agree. Also, Liuxiang tone 4 starts from an extremely high pitch; pronounced a little lower it is heard as tone 2. …
tone_statements.locator: p.18, sec. 1.2 声調; checked-syllable remark p.21 top; note 6 p.24

tone.says: Longhua Jiongnai has 8 tones, 44 33 53 31 35 11 55 12 (after Chen 1991), tones 7 and 8 on stop-final syllables; the Liuxiang variety has 9 values, 44 42 35 54 33 31 43 55 21 (tone 7 split 7a/7b).
